observations: Photo 0: a V-shaped automotive engine sitting on a paved/interlocked floor, person sitting on an orange plastic chair in background, no vehicle or chassis visible.
Photo 0 and 1: plastic engine cover bears embossed text 'PORSCHE' in large letters.
Photo 1: close-up of the same cover showing 'PORSCHE' logo clearly, oil residue/staining visible around valve cover gaskets.
Photo 2: another angle of the same engine, showing wiring harness, intake manifold runners, and a tan/beige component (possibly a reservoir or cover) with visible grime.
No VIN plate, engine code sticker, odometer, or chassis tag visible in any photo.
No test rig, stand with engine running, or multimeter/compression gauge shown.
Watermark 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' overlaid on all three photos - this is the seller's own branding, not independent proof.
Engine appears to be removed from a vehicle (pulled unit), resting directly on ground/pavement, with a cart and bare wheel rim in background suggesting a parts yard.

claims.claim: We also deals in all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: General business claim about seller's inventory range; no photo can confirm or deny this.

claims.claim: Implied: this is a genuine Porsche engine
claims.evidence: Brand name is molded into the plastic cover (photo 0, 1) which supports it being an OEM-style Porsche cover, but a cover alone does not confirm the internal engine block, nor which Porsche model it fits, nor that it is not a counterfeit/aftermarket cover.

risks.risk: Exact Porsche model/engine code is unreadable, and engine prices vary enormously between Porsche lines (e.g., Boxster/Cayenne V6 vs Panamera/Cayenne V8).
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code stamp/plate on the block, or a chassis/VIN tag from the donor car.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this, since worst-case and best-case prices differ by an order of magnitude

risks.risk: Running condition unknown - no start-up, compression, or leak-down evidence shown.
risks.proof: Video of the engine cranking/running with audio, or a compression/leak-down test readout.

risks.risk: Completeness unknown - turbochargers, sensors, wiring loom, ECU, accessories may be missing (only partial engine visible, no turbo units seen despite Porsche engines of this era often being turbocharged).
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set showing intake side, exhaust manifolds/turbo mounts, and accessory brackets.

risks.risk: Visible oil staining/residue around valve covers (photo 1) may indicate gasket leaks or prior internal issues.
risks.proof: Close-up of gasket mating surfaces after cleaning, or a pressure/leak test.

risks.risk: Mileage and service history of the donor vehicle are unknown.
risks.proof: Odometer photo from the donor car or service book/records.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the engine code/serial plate stamped on the block
A short video of the engine attempting to crank or run, with audible sound
Wide shots showing the intake manifold side and exhaust/turbo mounting points to assess completeness
Any donor-vehicle documentation (VIN, registration, or odometer photo) linking the engine to a specific Porsche model
response.reason: The brand 'Porsche' is legible on the cover but the specific model/engine code that sets the price is not readable in any photo, and running condition plus completeness are unverifiable, so even a worst-case price cannot be anchored without the engine code or donor-vehicle ID.
